engine.methodsNone: No scientific method in this version
engine.unavailable: Could not communicate with the calculation engine.

home.title: What would you like to do?

plan.title: Plan an experiment
plan.text: Define factors and responses and generate the run matrix.

analyze.title: Analyze existing data
analyze.text: Type or paste results you have already measured and summarize them.

compare.title: Compare treatments
compare.text: Compare the means of conditions or treatments.

availability.limited: Unavailable in this engine: the {{missing}} part is not registered in the loaded build. Update the app or reload the page.

home.recentEmpty: No recent projects. Projects opened or saved in the Windows app appear here; in the browser, use Open and choose the .enzitag file.
home.readyHint: Ready: use “Next” to continue with the chosen option.
home.recentHint: Or continue a project you already saved.

blocked.variables: Add at least one named response.
blocked.data: Enter at least one observation with a value and fix the cells with errors.

variables.title: Factors and responses
variables.intro: Factors are the conditions you vary or compare (for example, temperature or enzyme type). Responses are what you measure. You define the names and units.
variables.name: Name
variables.levelsHelp: Separate with semicolons, in the order you want. Empty: uses the labels found in the data, in alphabetical order.
variables.noFactors: No factors. You can summarize a response without factors.
variables.noResponses: No responses. Add at least one.

data.title: Data
data.intro: Type or paste the observations (from Excel, for example). Empty cells are missing data; numbers accept a dot or comma as the decimal separator.
data.caption: Observations table
data.showUnitHelp: Fill in the experimental unit only if you know which measurement belongs to which unit. The app does not assume that rows are independent replicates.
data.empty: No observations yet. Add a row or paste your data.
data.pasteNote: Tip: click a cell and paste (Ctrl+V). Several values copied from Excel fill the following cells.
data.pasteIgnored: {{count}} pasted column(s) beyond the last table column were ignored.
data.errorsSummary: {{count}} cell(s) with errors. Fix them before analyzing.
data.needColumns: Add factors and responses in the previous step to create the columns.

analysis.title: Analysis: descriptive summary
analysis.intro: Summarizes the chosen response with count, missing, mean, variance, standard deviation, minimum and maximum. This describes the data; it is not a comparison test.
analysis.groupByHelp: Check factors to summarize each combination of levels separately.

compare.title: Analysis: treatment comparison
compare.intro: Compares the means of a factor's levels: one-way ANOVA (completely randomised design), Tukey comparisons (Tukey–Kramer when group sizes differ) and comparison letters. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
compare.factorHelp: Each level of the factor forms a group. Rows without a response or without a level are left out and reported.
compare.alphaHelp: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons (simultaneous confidence 1 − α).
compare.needFactor: Add a factor (for example, the condition being tested) to define the groups.
compare.needLevels: Enter the factor levels in the variables step or type the data: at least two groups are required.

introFor.tukey: Compares the means of a factor's levels: one-way ANOVA (completely randomized design), Tukey comparisons (Tukey–Kramer when group sizes differ) and comparison letters. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.gamesHowell: Compares the means of a factor's levels without assuming equal variances: Welch ANOVA and Games–Howell comparisons, with comparison letters. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.dunnett: Compares each treatment with a control (Dunnett), starting from the one-way ANOVA. Choose the control level. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.bonferroni: Compares the means of a factor's levels with pairwise t tests adjusted by Bonferroni, starting from the one-way ANOVA. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.holm: Compares the means of a factor's levels with pairwise t tests adjusted by Holm, starting from the one-way ANOVA. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.kruskalDunn: Compares the groups without assuming normality: Kruskal–Wallis and Dunn comparisons. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.factorial: Fits the ANOVA with several factors and/or blocks, in the model chosen below, and compares the means of each effect with the chosen multiplicity adjustment. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.

alphaHelpFor.tukey: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons (simultaneous confidence 1 − α).
alphaHelpFor.gamesHowell: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons (simultaneous confidence 1 − α).
alphaHelpFor.dunnett: Applies to the family of comparisons of each treatment with the control (simultaneous confidence 1 − α).
alphaHelpFor.bonferroni: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons, with the Bonferroni adjustment.
alphaHelpFor.holm: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons, with the Holm adjustment.
alphaHelpFor.kruskalDunn: Applies to the global test and to the family of Dunn pairwise comparisons.
alphaHelpFor.factorial: Applies to the ANOVA and to the family of comparisons of each effect.

design.title: Analysis: two-level design
design.intro: Estimates effects and coefficients on the coded scale (−1, +1), with Pareto, main effects, interactions and observed vs predicted. Without error degrees of freedom only Lenth's method flags active effects, and it is labelled as such.
design.needDesign: Generate the design in the data step (or open a project that contains it).
design.modelHelp: Terms aliased with each other (fractional designs) appear as not estimable.
design.curvatureUnavailable: The design has no centre points.

surface.title: Analysis: response surface
surface.intro: Fits the second-order model (main effects, quadratic terms and two-factor interactions) on the coded scale and shows ANOVA, lack of fit, equation and surface.
surface.needFactors: The surface needs at least two quantitative factors with numeric values.
surface.modelHelp: Terms can be removed manually; the app never drops terms on its own. Quadratic terms and interactions without the matching main effect are flagged.
surface.asSurfaceHelp: Use for custom or imported matrices with quantitative factors; the coded scale uses the lowest and highest value of each factor.
surface.needDesign: Generate the design in the data step.

help.tukey: Default: all pairs, assuming equal variances.
help.gamesHowell: Use when groups have very different variances or sizes.
help.dunnett: Use when only each treatment against the control matters.
help.bonferroni: All pairs with pooled variance; conservative.
help.kruskalDunn: Use when data are not normally distributed or are ordinal.

method.blockHelp: The block enters as an additive effect (no interaction) and removes between-block variation from the error.
method.ssHelp: With balanced data the three types agree; with unbalanced data, type III tests each term after all others and type II respects model hierarchy.
method.contrastsHelp: Define a linear combination of one factor's means (coefficients sum to zero), for example 1; -0.5; -0.5.
method.contrastInvalid: Enter a name and {{count}} numeric coefficients (one per factor level).

project.name: Project name
project.saveBrowserHelp: In the browser, saving downloads the .enzitag file; the previous file is not replaced.
project.confirmDiscard: There are changes not saved to a file. Continue and lose those changes?
project.failed: The operation could not be completed. The open project was not changed.
project.migrated: File from format version {{from}}, upgraded in memory; the original file was not changed.

status.title: Saving status
status.unsaved: Changes not saved to a file
status.recoveryPending: waiting for a 2 s pause in editing…
status.recoveryError: unavailable in this browser; your changes are not protected
status.recoveryNote: It stays in this browser; it is not an external backup.

recovery.title: Unsaved session found
recovery.text: There is a session with unsaved changes, kept in this browser at {{time}}. Restore it?

history.title: Version history
history.intro: Each version is a snapshot of the data created when importing, analyzing, saving or restoring. Nothing is deleted automatically.
history.restoreNote: Restoring creates a new version; the current one stays in the history.

import.title: Import data
import.intro: Review the preview, choose each column's role and confirm. The current data stays in the version history.
import.encodingFallback: The file was not valid UTF-8; it was read as Windows-1252. Check the accents in the preview.
import.header: The first row contains the column names
import.replaceNote: The current data of this experiment will be replaced; it stays in the version history.
import.unitHelp: Rows with the same experimental unit are repeated measurements of that unit, not independent replicates.
import.failed: The file could not be read:
import.formulaNote: Spreadsheets: only stored values are read; formulas are never executed.
import.nothing: Nothing to import: choose at least one column as a factor or response.

fill.title: Fill in the design responses
fill.intro: This file has the factors and responses of this experiment (for example, the collection sheet exported from the run matrix). Each line is matched to the run with the same levels (or the same unit) and only the responses are written; the design and the factors stay as they are.
fill.modeLegend: What to do with the file
fill.modeFill: Fill in only the responses of the current experiment (recommended)
fill.modeReplace: Replace all data with this file
fill.summary: {{filled}} response value(s) will be written; {{empty}} blank cell(s) in the file are left as they are.
fill.replacing: {{count}} value(s) already entered will be replaced; the previous state stays in the version history.
fill.unmatched: {{count}} line(s) of the file match no run (levels differ from the planned ones, or the run was already used) and will not be written. Lines: {{lines}}.
fill.invalid: {{count}} response cell(s) are not numbers and must be fixed in the file. Lines: {{lines}}.
fill.rowsWithoutLine: {{count}} run(s) of the experiment have no line in the file and stay as they are.
fill.keeps: Factors, run order and design do not change.

design.title: Experiment design
design.intro: Generates the two-level run matrix for factor screening. Each factor must be quantitative, with a low and a high level. The run count is shown before generating.
design.needFactors: Add at least two quantitative factors (with a name) in the previous step.
design.categoricalIgnored: Categorical factors are not part of a two-level design: {{names}}.
design.levelsInvalid: The low level must be smaller than the high level (numbers).
design.budgetHelp: Counts the basic design only, without replicates or centre points.
design.replicatesHelp: Each repetition redoes every run. They are experimental replicates only if each run is a new independent preparation.
design.centerHelp: They allow testing for curvature. A single centre point gives no error estimate.
design.seedHelp: The same seed gives the same order on Windows and in the browser.
design.countError: The runs could not be counted.
design.confirmReplace: Replace the current runs with the new matrix? The current data stay in the version history.
design.generated: Design generated: {{total}} runs. Fill in the responses in the grid below.

matrix.title: Run matrix
matrix.failed: The matrix could not be exported.

properties.title: Properties
properties.aliasesHelp: Effects on the same line cannot be separated by this design: what is estimated is their sum.
properties.pbPartial: Plackett–Burman: main effects are partially aliased with two-factor interactions (maximum absolute correlation {{value}}).
properties.dummy: {{count}} dummy columns (contrasts not used by factors): they remain as error degrees of freedom.
properties.axial: Central composite: α = {{alpha}}; {{factorial}} factorial points, {{axial}} axial and {{center}} centre points.

surface.intro: Central composite and Box–Behnken designs estimate curvature (quadratic terms). Use them after screening, with the factors that matter. Centre points are needed to estimate pure error.
surface.custom: Central composite with a given α
surface.inscribed: Inscribed: axial points sit at the stated levels and the factorial part inside them
surface.inscribedHelp: Circumscribed (default): the factorial part sits at the stated levels and the axial points beyond them, at ±α.
surface.cubeGeneratorsHelp: Comma-separated generators, for example E=ABCD. Empty: full factorial.
surface.centerSuggested: Centre points set to 5 (needed for pure error).

mode.rcbd: One categorical factor in blocks (randomized RCBD)

crd.intro: Completely randomized design: one factor with several treatments (levels), the same number of independent experimental units in each, and a run order drawn with a recorded seed.
crd.needFactor: Add a named categorical factor in the previous step to plan the CRD.
crd.levelsHelp: Separate with semicolons or line breaks, for example: Control; pH 5; pH 7. The levels are stored on the factor.
crd.replicatesHelp: Each unit is an independent preparation or sample. Measuring the same sample several times does not create a new unit.
crd.unitNote: Each run gets an experimental-unit identifier (for example T2-R3: level 2, unit 3).

rcbd.intro: Randomized complete block design: each block (day, batch, operator…) gets every treatment once, in an order drawn within the block. Between-block variation is removed from the error.
rcbd.needFactors: Add two named categorical factors in the previous step: one for the treatments and one for the blocks.
rcbd.randomize: Randomize the order within each block
rcbd.unitNote: Each run gets a unit identifier (for example B2-T3: block 2, treatment 3). The analysis uses the block as an additive effect.

design.collectionNote: Collection sheet: the exported file has an empty column for each response. Fill it in at the lab and import the same file with “Import file”: only the responses are written, into the matching runs.

mixed.title: Mixed-levels factorial
mixed.intro: Combines every level of two or more factors with different numbers of levels (for example 3 strains × 2 pH values × 4 agitation speeds), with replicates and a run order drawn with a recorded seed. The analysis is the multi-factor ANOVA, with marginal means and contrasts.
mixed.needFactors: In the previous step, add at least two named factors with two or more levels typed in the «Levels» field.
mixed.levelsHelp: Each factor's levels are stored on the factor itself, separated by semicolons or line breaks. Numeric factors enter as named levels.
mixed.matrix: Run order of the mixed-levels factorial

mixture.title: Mixture design
mixture.intro: Components are proportions that sum to 1. The simplex-lattice {q, m} uses the combinations of proportions that are multiples of 1/m; the simplex-centroid uses every subset of components in equal parts. Lower bounds shrink the region (pseudo-components). Upper bounds are not handled yet.
mixture.needFactors: In the previous step, add at least two named numeric factors: each is the proportion of one mixture component.
mixture.lowerHelp: The lower bounds must sum to less than 1. Leave 0 when there is no bound.

warn.no_pure_error: Without replicates or extra center points there is no pure error to test lack of fit.

optimal.title: D- and I-optimal design
optimal.intro: Chooses, from a grid of candidates inside your constraints, the runs that best estimate the model: D maximizes the information on the coefficients; I minimizes the average prediction variance over the region. Useful for irregular regions, a fixed number of runs and for augmenting runs already done.
optimal.needFactors: In the previous step, add at least one named numeric factor.
optimal.needRanges: Enter the low and high limits (numbers) of every chosen factor.
optimal.levels: Levels per factor in the grid
optimal.constraints: Linear constraints (sum of coefficient × value ≤ limit, in real units)
optimal.constraintHelp: Example: coefficients 1 and 1 with limit 40 mean factor 1 + factor 2 ≤ 40. Leave blank the coefficient of a factor that does not take part.
optimal.augment: Augment: keep the {{count}} runs already done (rows with numeric factors and a response)
optimal.randomize: Randomize the run order of the new runs
optimal.summary: {{runs}} runs chosen from {{candidates}} candidates; the best value was reached in {{reached}} of {{starts}} starts.
optimal.noGlobal: The search is local with several starts: the design is very good for the criterion, but the application does not guarantee the global optimum.
optimal.apply: Use this design in the data
optimal.applied: {{count}} new runs went to the data grid; the analysis will be a response surface (choose the model terms in the result).
optimal.excluded: Left out of the optimal design: {{names}}. This version only handles numeric factors in the D/I-optimal design; {{count}} categorical factor(s) are not in the matrix and their columns stay empty.
optimal.confirmEmpty: These columns will be empty in the data grid: {{names}}. You will have to fill them in before analyzing. Use the design anyway?
optimal.appliedEmpty: Fill in the columns that were left empty in the grid: {{names}}.

optimization.title: Desirability optimization
optimization.intro: Set the goal of each response (preference) and, if needed, mandatory limits. The search uses the second-order models fitted to your data, starts from many points and presents candidates with predictions and intervals. It does not guarantee the global optimum: confirm the candidates with new runs.
optimization.stale: The data or the setup changed since this search: run it again to refresh the candidates.
optimization.convergence: Search: {{starts}} starts (seed {{seed}}); {{converged}} converged by tolerance; {{feasible}} ended at feasible points; {{distinct}} distinct solution(s); the best was found by {{best}} starts.

status.found: Feasible candidates with positive desirability were found.
status.onlyZeroDesirability: There are feasible points, but none with positive desirability: the goals cannot be met together in the region. The candidates below are the closest.
status.infeasible: No point of the region satisfies the mandatory limits: there is no feasible candidate.

goals.title: Response goals
goals.help: Preferences (goal and importance) are combined into a global desirability; mandatory limits (minimum or maximum predicted value) remove points and are not traded off against other responses.
goals.importanceHelp: Relative weight in the global desirability (default 1).
goals.limitHelp: Leave empty if there is no limit.

goal.targetHelp: Desirability is 1 from (or up to) this value.
goal.shapeHelp: 1 = linear; greater than 1 demands getting closer to the target.

domain.title: Search domain
domain.region: Experimental region (default): the factor ranges actually run, no extrapolation
domain.extended: Extend the factor limits (extrapolation, by explicit choice)
domain.help: Outside the experimental region the model has not been tested: candidates outside it are marked as extrapolation.

search.title: Advanced search options
search.startsHelp: More starts give more confidence that the best candidate is not a local optimum (1 to 5000).
search.seedHelp: The same seed gives the same candidates.

run.cancelled: Search cancelled; the previous results were kept.
run.needResponse: Include at least one response in the optimization.

candidates.caption: Candidates (real conditions and, in parentheses, coded)

tradeoffs.title: Trade-offs between responses
tradeoffs.help: Best desirability each response would reach alone (same constraints). In the candidates, the number in parentheses is how much individual desirability was given up.

view.heading: Global desirability over two factors
view.title: Global desirability
view.description: Global desirability as a function of two factors, with the others fixed at the best candidate's conditions.
view.reading: Lines: global desirability; darker = more desirable.
view.sameAxis: Choose different factors on the two axes.

confirmation.title: Confirmation runs
confirmation.intro: Choose candidates and replicates: the app creates a new experiment, linked to this one, with the conditions rounded to 5 significant digits and the predictions stored to compare with what is observed.

check.title: Check against the predictions
check.help: Predictions stored with the proposal, with a {{level}}% prediction interval.
check.note: A value inside the interval is compatible with the model; outside it, the model may not describe these conditions well. With few runs the conclusion is limited.

update.current: You already have the latest version.
update.failed: Could not check right now (no internet or service unavailable).
update.safe: The update is installed only if its signature matches the app's key. Your projects are your own files and are not changed.
update.notes: What is new in this version

channelHelp.experimental: Receives every published version, including the 0.x series. It is the only channel until version 1.0.0 exists.
channelHelp.stable: Receives stable versions only (from 1.0.0). Until then this channel has no versions and the check will report that it could not verify.

analysis.title: Mixture analysis (Scheffé models)
analysis.intro: Fits the chosen model without an intercept on the pseudo-components. The ANOVA uses the mean-centered total sum of squares. The result is computed on request and is not stored in the project.
analysis.note: No intercept: the linear terms already carry the average level. Coefficients are in pseudo-components; predictions are valid only inside the design region.
analysis.badCells: Some responses are not numbers in rows {{rows}}.

repeated.title: Repeated measures, paired data and mixed models
repeated.intro: For data that are not independent: the same unit measured under two conditions (paired) or several times (repeated measures, lots, days). Both tools use the «Unit» column of the data grid. Results are computed on request and are not stored in the project.
repeated.needUnits: No row has an experimental unit. Show the «Unit» column and fill it in (for example, the subject or lot identifier).
repeated.showUnitColumn: Show the «Unit» column in the grid

paired.title: Paired comparison (two conditions)
paired.needTwoLevels: Needs a categorical factor with exactly two levels in the data.
paired.noPairs: No unit has both conditions with a response. Check the “Experimental unit” chosen above and that each unit was measured in both conditions.
paired.incomplete: Units left out because they have only one of the conditions: {{units}}.
paired.duplicated: Units left out because they have more than one observation at the same level: {{units}}.
paired.withoutUnit: {{count}} row(s) without a unit were ignored.
paired.note: The paired t assumes roughly normal differences; Wilcoxon drops zero differences and uses mid-ranks for ties.

mixed.title: Mixed model (random intercept per unit)
mixed.boundary: The between-unit variance is zero (boundary): the model is equivalent to one without the random effect and the degrees of freedom are the residual ones.
mixed.note: REML estimation with compound symmetry (all measures of a unit share the same correlation). AR(1) and unstructured covariances are not available yet.

unit.label: Experimental unit
unit.help: The individual, batch or plot measured more than once. Choose a factor if the unit is already in it.
unit.summary: {{complete}} unit(s) with both conditions form a pair; {{incomplete}} incomplete and {{duplicated}} with a repeat in the same level are left out.
unit.sameAsPair: The experimental unit cannot be the same factor that defines the two conditions.

saturation.title: Saturation curves (Monod, Michaelis–Menten, Haldane and Hill)
saturation.intro: Fits rate or growth against substrate by nonlinear least squares (Levenberg–Marquardt, several starts). The substrate is a numeric factor and the response is one of the responses. The result is computed on request and is not stored in the project.
saturation.needFactor: Add a numeric factor (the substrate) to fit a saturation curve.
saturation.badCells: Some values are not numbers in rows {{rows}}.
saturation.starts: {{reached}} of {{run}} starts reached the best fit.
saturation.chartLabel: Fitted saturation curve with the observed points and the confidence band

warn.not_converged: The fit did not converge within the iteration limit: do not use these values.
warn.parameter_at_bound: A parameter ended at a (positivity) bound: the model may not suit the data.
warn.ill_conditioned: The information matrix is ill-conditioned: parameters cannot be identified separately.
warn.highly_correlated: Two parameters are correlated above 0.99: the data do not separate them (substrate range too narrow).
warn.imprecise_parameter: A standard error is more than ten times the estimate: the parameter is practically undetermined.
warn.few_degrees_of_freedom: Few degrees of freedom: the intervals are unreliable.
warn.single_start_best: Only one start reached the best fit: confirm with runs at other concentrations.

saturation.note: Wald intervals (approximation). The fit only holds inside the measured substrate range; identifying Ks and μmax needs measurements below and above Ks.
saturation.stale: This fit is for other inputs (factor, response, model or data): fit again to update it.

power.title: Power and sample size calculator
power.intro: Use it before the runs: how many units are needed to detect an expected difference, or what power a sample has. The formulas are exact (noncentral F and t distributions). The result depends on the standard deviation and the effect you assume.
power.note: Power holds for the σ and effect entered. If the real σ is larger, power will be lower; consider a margin.
power.stale: This result is for other values: a field changed after calculating. Calculate again to update it.

drive.title: Google Drive (optional)
drive.intro: Save and open your projects in Google Drive. Nothing is sent until you connect, and the app only sees the «EnziTAG Optima» folder and the files it created or that you choose to open (drive.file scope).
drive.linked: Project linked to the Drive file «{{name}}».
drive.unlinked: This project is not in Drive yet: «Save to Drive» creates the file in the «EnziTAG Optima» folder.
drive.created: File «{{name}}» created in the «EnziTAG Optima» folder of your Drive.
drive.conflict: The file was changed in Drive after your last read, so it was **not overwritten**. Your work was saved as «{{copy}}» in the same folder; open both and compare before deleting either.
drive.localStillWorks: Drive is optional: saving and opening files on your computer keep working as usual.
drive.desktopNote: The Windows version does not have Google Drive integration yet; use the web version or save to your computer.

errors.auth: Google authorization expired or was refused. Connect again.
errors.permission: No permission for this file in Drive.
errors.rateLimit: Google rate-limited the requests. Try again in a few minutes.
errors.notFound: The file was not found in Drive (deleted or outside the app's reach).
errors.network: No connection to Google. Your work stays in the app; try again when you are online.
errors.unknown: Drive returned an unexpected error. Your work stays in the app.

comments.intro: Review notes are stored in the project, linked to the analysis or figure and to the data revision they were written against. Figure comments are written on the figure itself.
comments.author: Your name (optional, stays on this device only)
comments.confirmDelete: Delete this comment and its replies?
